userStories.title: Disclose the bypassPermissions default in a README security section
userStories.description: As a prospective user evaluating the project in public, I need the README to state up front that the default permission mode runs the agent without permission prompts and to name the container-isolation alternative, so that the security posture is disclosed by us rather than discovered by a hostile reader.
acceptanceCriteria: The README gains a first-level security section heading. [oracle: grep -qiE '^#+ .*security' README.md]

The section names the actual default permission mode, and that claim still matches the code's source of truth, re-checked in the same clause. [oracle: grep -q 'bypassPermissions' README.md && grep -q "DEFAULT_PERMISSION_MODE = 'bypassPermissions'" src/config/permission-mode.ts]
The section explains what the default DOES (the agent runs without a permission prompt), not merely that a flag exists. [oracle: grep -qi 'permission prompt' README.md]
The section names the container-isolation alternative by its real config key so a reader can act on it. [oracle: grep -q 'worker_isolation' README.md && grep -qi container README.md]

The disclosure reads as an honest, self-contained paragraph a hostile reader could not improve on by discovering the default themselves: it states the default, its consequence, and the mitigation. [oracle: reviewer-judgment]

The rest of the README is preserved and not truncated by the insertion, with the length comparand re-derived live from main in the same clause. [oracle: grep -q '^## License' README.md && test "$(git show main:README.md | wc -l)" -le "$(wc -l < README.md)"]

userStories.notes: File: README.md only. This is must-fix #1 of docs/launch-readiness.md. The measured fact to carry: src/config/permission-mode.ts exports DEFAULT_PERMISSION_MODE = 'bypassPermissions', applied when ~/.config/cam/config.toml is missing or the key is unset, and it is what `cam init` writes. The mitigation to name: `[loop] worker_isolation = "container"` in scripts/cam/project.toml (see src/commands/setup.ts:168 and src/config/models.ts:454 for the exact accepted values container|host, default host). README lines 155-158 already say the permission mode is read from ~/.config/cam/config.toml and that no subcommand exposes a flag for it: place the new section so it complements those lines instead of contradicting them, and keep the never-add-a---permission-mode-flag invariant intact (do not document a flag that must never exist). Evidence fidelity: the text must carry the measured fact, not just the flag name.

findings.text: The diff replaced a true comment with a false one: line 11 now claims the identity panel "reads as the Gateship brand identity", but the panel renders the ASCII "CAM" wordmark (:117-119) plus a literal bold "Runtime" line (:120-122), i.e. the running binary's splash still displays the dead name "CAM Runtime". Verified by rendering the real component with ink-testing-library (frame captured in scripts/cam/review-artifact.txt section 3), not by reading the comment. This is the lying-surface defect class US-005 exists to close, and the splash test's own header (test/ui/splash.test.tsx:5-6) codifies the invariant "never assert behavior from a comment". Fix by either rewording lines 10-11 to state what actually renders (and naming CAM-421/CAM-331 as the owner of the visual identity), or renaming the rendered "Runtime" text line, which is a plain display string like index.ts:114 and run.ts:786 and not the wordmark art the PRD deferred.

CHANGELOG.md line 3 still reads "All notable changes to CAM Runtime are documented here". That is a live statement, not rewritten history (unlike the historical entries at :604-612, which must stay), and it is a public-repo landing surface carrying the dead name. Out of this PRD's declared scope, so non-blocking, but worth a one-line follow-up before any public amplification.

The Security disclosure sits at line 301 of 347, after Architecture and just before Recent changes. US-004's story description asks for the posture to be stated "up front" for a prospective evaluator; every acceptance criterion is met, but a hostile reader scanning the top of the README would still not meet it. Consider hoisting the section near Prerequisites/Install.

The CLI tagline keeps main's old category prose with only the name swapped ("Gateship: a local software-delivery runtime for coding agents"), while README.md:3 adopts docs/positioning.md:7 ("a local software delivery runtime: a control plane for coding agents"). US-001's notes asked for the positioning sentence rather than invented prose, so the CLI and README now state the category differently and hyphenate it differently.

No test guards the rename: nothing under test/ references Gateship, and no assertion fails if the dead name returns to index.ts, run.ts, or config.ts. The grep oracles live only in prd.json, which is per-cycle state. A one-file ratchet mirroring test/no-permission-mode-flag.test.ts would make the sweep durable.
